source.title: Abhinavagupta: self-awareness is nature of consciousness, not result of cognition
source.author: Codex/Hermes loop

claims.claim_text: Self-awareness (svasaṃvedana) is the nature (svabhāva) of consciousness, not a result (phala) of cognition. Consciousness is self-luminous (svaprakāśa) and is its own object of awareness; it is not an object of a means of knowledge other than its own self-awareness. The Buddhist phala-model makes self-awareness dependent on cognition, contradicting its self-luminous nature.
claims.hetu: consciousness is self-luminous and its own object, not dependent on external means of knowledge
claims.sadhya: self-awareness is the nature of consciousness, not a produced result
claims.vyapti_statement: If consciousness is self-luminous and self-aware by nature, then self-awareness is its svabhāva, not a phala of cognition.

falsifier.condition: Show that the Buddhist phala-model of svasaṃvitti is compatible with svaprakāśa — that a result-of-cognition can also be the nature of consciousness without contradiction.
